data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘durga’ (fortress) and ‘iswar’ (lord), Durgeswar represents the lord of all fortresses or the protector. In Hindu mythology, Durga is a powerful goddess and the embodiment of female energy, and Durgeswar is her male counterpart. The name Durgeswar carries the meaning “God of Fortresses” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Durgeswar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of fortresses and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, protection, and the divine power that guards and upholds the universe.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Durgeswar total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Durgeswar holds significant cultural significance within the Hindu community, reflecting the belief in the protective deity. This name is often given to newborns to invoke the blessings of Durga, the goddess of strength and power. Many Hindu temples and most importantly, the famous Durga Puja festivals are dedicated to the worship of Durga and Durgeswar, emphasizing the importance of seeking shelter and protection in God.
data.spiritual_significance: Durgeswar is a name that embodies the divine masculine aspect of the universal protective deity, emphasizing the essence of protection, strength, and courage. This name serves as a reminder that no matter what challenges we may face in life, there is always a divine power that can provide shelter and protection. For Hindus, Durgeswar represents a direct connection to the ultimate giver of strength and protection during hardships and trials.
